scope: Proposition 5.6 (Insertion of a pair of simple primes) of the manuscript “Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves” (preprints/Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 006 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c417858c9fe566da), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 31. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose E(Q)[2] ̸= 0 and U has matching parity. Let a rational elementary label, relative to S and all existing split vertices, be realized by a simple prime q with #E(Fq) ≡ 2 (mod 4). Inserting two fresh simple primes with this same label leaves A(U) unchanged. Their mutual simple-edge label, and their labels against other simple vertices, do not affect this assertion.
